chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no righteous servant who is insulted, so he says, “I am fasting. Peace be upon you. I shall not insult you just as you have insulted me,” except that the Lord, Blessed and High, says: “My servant sought protection with fasting from the evil of My servant, so I have protected him from the Fire.”'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit for a fasting person who responds to insults by saying 'I am fasting'?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the metaphysical efficacy of fasting as a divine shield against spiritual harm. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and the unique status of the fasting servant, where the physical act of abstention becomes a direct invocation for protection from the Hellfire, as affirmed by God's own declaration.
